thesis: Preserving an artwork’s perceptible material can frustrate the temporal relations that give it value. Care can therefore require allowing a performance to finish. This does not establish a general requirement of irreversible disappearance: preservation decisions must distinguish completion, repeatability, truthful knowledge of finality, and any independently justified artistic value of that finality.
contribution: The manuscript offers a useful conceptual clarification of preservation. Its strongest established result concerns the sound staircase: sustaining its last state defeats the described movement toward ordinary listening, whereas recording complete performances need not. The sculpture establishes a different, narrower result: reproducing appearances does not necessarily reproduce the spectator’s truthful situation. Together these distinctions support more accurate descriptions of preservation choices. They do not establish that irreversible destruction has artistic value in the second example, or provide a general decision rule for sacrificing future access.
argument_map: Body paragraphs 2–6: The staircase directs attention through diminishing sounds toward the surrounding world. Indefinitely sustaining its seventh note prevents that transition. Given this account of the work’s organization, retaining one audible component frustrates the realization of the whole.

Paragraphs 5–9: Artist intention alone cannot establish the necessity of disappearance. The relevant consideration is what an ending contributes to valued relations within the work. The Aristotle reference supplies an analogy concerning parts and wholes, expressly not a general prohibition on restoration.

Paragraphs 10–11: A recording can preserve the sequence while allowing every performance to finish. Thus the staircase supports completion, not the elimination of recordings or future performances. The manuscript explicitly accepts this objection and restricts its conclusion.

Paragraphs 12–13: Truthfully knowing that a particular object will never return changes the spectator’s choices and situation. Secret preservation makes the relevant belief false; disclosed preservation changes its content. However, this difference alone establishes neither artistic merit nor an aesthetic reason for permanent loss.

Paragraphs 14–17: Future access and fairness can justify preservation. Where finality has independently established artistic value, preservation may involve an aesthetic sacrifice; otherwise that cost remains unproven. Museums should describe whether they retain a work, transform it, or preserve testimony to its completion.

strongest_merit.location: Body paragraphs 10–15, especially paragraph 11 beginning «Для описанной лестницы»
strongest_merit.reason: The manuscript identifies and accepts the decisive recording objection, then distinguishes performance completion from irreversible unavailability. This is substantive because it changes what the original example licenses. Its subsequent separation of a changed spectator situation from demonstrated artistic value also prevents the sculpture from covertly restoring the rejected inference. The resulting distinctions remain useful even without endorsing destruction.

concerns.excerpt: Перед нами может быть прекрасная вещь, но её достоинство уже другое.
concerns.reason: The proposed test is persuasive for this stipulated staircase but underdetermined as a preservation criterion. Altering relations responsible for some value does not by itself show that preservation has failed: interpretation and restoration can also change valued relations. The text needs a distinction between relations necessary to realizing the relevant work and relations that may legitimately vary. This limits application beyond the unusually clear example without defeating its local conclusion.
concerns.text_response: Paragraph 5 rejects mere obedience to the artist; paragraph 6 appeals to the organization of the whole; paragraph 7 explicitly denies that the Aristotle analogy prohibits restoration. These qualifications acknowledge the problem but do not supply the missing distinction.
concerns.discriminating_check: Compare indefinitely sustaining the last note with changing its duration while still completing the transition to ambient listening. Explain why the first frustrates a constitutive relation while the second can remain an acceptable realization, without relying solely on authorial instruction.

concerns.location: Body paragraphs 12–16, especially paragraph 13 beginning «Это не доказывает»
concerns.excerpt: Для этой скульптуры такого доказательства пока нет.
concerns.reason: The irreversible sculpture establishes a difference in truthful spectator circumstances, but the manuscript expressly leaves its artistic significance unestablished. Consequently, the second half supplies a diagnostic distinction rather than a demonstrated aesthetic conflict between finality and future access. That is a defensible modest contribution, but its practical importance remains limited until the distinction identifies an artistic cost beyond scarcity or disappointed expectations. This is an acknowledged boundary, not a concealed contradiction or fatal failure.
concerns.text_response: Paragraph 13 explicitly distinguishes meaningful experience from ticket scarcity. Paragraph 15 makes aesthetic sacrifice conditional on an additional justification and permits preservation for accessibility or fairness. Paragraph 16 therefore offers accurate description rather than a mandatory conservation outcome.
concerns.discriminating_check: Develop contrasting cases where truthful irreversibility respectively organizes a defensible artistic achievement and merely creates scarcity. Show what evidence supports the difference and how it changes the stated costs of preservation, even if future access ultimately outweighs them.

originality_limit: The packet supports assessment of the argument’s internal distinctions, but not a reliable originality score. Its single Aristotle reference supplies a historical analogy, not evidence of novelty relative to work on performance, conservation, or ephemeral art. The combination may be useful without being demonstrably new.
reason_ru: Эссе полезно различает сохранение материала, завершение исполнения и необратимую утрату.
Его довод помогает точнее объяснить, что музей сохраняет и что меняет.
Рекомендация пограничная: результат убедителен, но узок; художественная ценность невозвратности здесь не доказана, а новизна не установлена.
limits: The complete supplied manuscript and bibliography were read. Paragraph numbering starts with «В городе» and excludes the title.
External source correctness and exhaustive novelty were not checked. No browsing or independent source verification was performed.
The review assesses the fictional examples as philosophical arguments; the packet supplies no independently examined conservation cases.
